summary: Rialto sits on the valley floor of the San Bernardino basin, flat and sun-drenched, with the San Gabriel and San Bernardino Mountains forming a dramatic wall to the north — on clear winter days after rain scrubs the air, those peaks carry snow while daytime highs still hover in the 60s. With roughly 9.6 hours of sunshine per day on average and annual highs around 77°F, summer heat is real (triple digits are routine in July and August), but the dry air means evenings cool sharply into the mid-50s year-round. At a median home value of $454,400 against a median household income of $85,521, the price-to-income ratio lands around 5.3 — tight but measurably more accessible than most of coastal Southern California. Rialto functions largely as a bedroom community; the I-10 and I-210 freeways bracket the city, and the sprawling logistics and warehouse corridor along the I-15 in neighboring Fontana and San Bernardino provides a significant share of local employment, alongside healthcare and public-sector jobs at county facilities. The street grid is classic Inland Empire — wide arterials connecting residential tracts, with commercial strips rather than a walkable downtown core, and open desert-edge terrain to the north offering proximity to trails in the San Bernardino National Forest. Rialto is a place where Inland Empire affordability and mountain-framed geography coexist with the commute-dependent, car-first trade-offs that define the region.
